cards.stem: What was the approximate cost for each acre in the transaction described?
cards.quote: For roughly 4 cents an acre, the United States doubled its size, expanding the nation westward.
cards.hint: Think about the per acre price mentioned early on

cards.stem: How much was paid for the land west of the Mississippi River?
cards.quote: the United States purchased 828,000 square miles of land west of the Mississippi River for $15 million
cards.hint: Recall the total sum noted for the large tract

cards.stem: What did the growth of the country bring to light between the North and South?
options: sectional weaknesses between the North and South
cards.quote: also exposed the sectional weaknesses between the North and South, especially related to the issue of slavery
cards.hint: Consider what divisions were revealed by expansion

cards.stem: What ultimately happened to Native people as new lands were organized?
cards.quote: Ultimately, Native people were forcibly moved on to reservations, losing vast acreage of their tribal lands
cards.hint: Remember the consequence for Indigenous communities

every card has distinct options after normalisation (options-distinct)
no stem contains its own correct answer (stem-no-answer-leak)
exactly one option per card matches the quote (one-correct)
every number in stems, options and hints appears on the cited page or in the same quote as that whole signed number (N-01) (numbers-checkable)
no distractor occurs in its card quote (distractors-not-in-quote)
